specification.title: A unique violation is caught inside the transaction, which then ends normally
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Write the marker `tx`, and make sure the write was sent to PostgreSQL.
Checkpoint `after-write`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(), read through the transaction's own connection.

Insert the value 'taken' into uniq through the framework's ordinary write API. It fails with unique_violation (23505). Catch the error and continue. After catching the error, the callback sends nothing else and returns.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report the same backend PID. The transaction is aborted, so it cannot run queries; the runner confirms the aborted state server-side.
End the transaction normally, so that the framework sends COMMIT.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: When PostgreSQL has aborted the transaction before it ends, so that its COMMIT is answered with ROLLBACK, the API does not report a successful commit.

execution.description: Database.BeginTransactionAsync, CommitAsync, and RollbackAsync. Marker inserts use Database.ExecuteSqlAsync. The native TX-01A violation is SaveChangesAsync, which EF Core wraps in a savepoint. Nested scopes use CreateSavepointAsync. Pooling is false. EnableRetryOnFailure is not called. The provider's default execution strategy is left in place.

configuration.writes: Database.ExecuteSqlAsync for markers; SaveChangesAsync for the native TX-01A unique violation
configuration.savepoints: CreateSavepointAsync, RollbackToSavepointAsync, ReleaseSavepointAsync; SaveChangesAsync may create its own savepoint
configuration.execution_strategy: the provider default; EnableRetryOnFailure is not called

execution.form: Database.BeginTransactionAsync returns the handle. The application calls CommitAsync or RollbackAsync. Marker inserts are Database.ExecuteSqlAsync so the row is written in the top-level transaction. SaveChangesAsync is the native TX-01A violation.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A unique_violation raised by PostgreSQL inside the transaction, and caught by the application.
fault.injection_point: After the first write, before the transaction ends.
fault.preconditions: The row 'taken' already exists in uniq (fixture).
fault.expected_server: The failed statement aborts the transaction. PostgreSQL answers the later COMMIT with the command tag ROLLBACK, without an error, and commits nothing.
fault.expected_client: The driver receives the command tag ROLLBACK as the reply to COMMIT.

knowledge: The outcome reaches the client: PostgreSQL's reply to COMMIT carries the command tag ROLLBACK.

api_outcome.contract: EF Core 10 IDbContextTransaction.CommitAsync commits the transaction begun by Database.BeginTransactionAsync. The EF Core transaction API does not return a PostgreSQL command tag. A return from CommitAsync is reported as committed. A throw from CommitAsync is reported as failed. A throw from the body followed by RollbackAsync returning is reported as rolled_back. A throw from RollbackAsync is reported as failed. Marker inserts use Database.ExecuteSqlAsync. SaveChangesAsync inside an explicit transaction inserts the row under a savepoint and releases it; the row xmin is then that subtransaction, while pg_current_xact_id() is the top-level id, and the harness does not attribute that xmin to a top-level write. The native TX-01A violation is still SaveChangesAsync of a Uniq entity. The execute-sql mode uses ExecuteSqlAsync for that violation. A nested scope is CreateSavepointAsync, RollbackToSavepointAsync, and ReleaseSavepointAsync. EF Core creates its own savepoint around SaveChangesAsync when a user transaction is already active and the transaction reports SupportsSavepoints. This adapter does not disable that savepoint and does not read Npgsql protocol messages.

violation.message: An error occurred while saving the entity changes. See the inner exception for details.

preconditions.description: the write of marker "tx" had reached PostgreSQL at `after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the duplicate insert failed with unique_violation (23505), as reported by the adapter
the top-level transaction was aborted before it ended: at `before-end` the session was "idle in transaction (aborted)" and pg_xact_status() already reported it aborted
preconditions.detail: state: "idle in transaction"; pg_xact_status: in progress

preconditions.description: PostgreSQL did not commit the transaction

evaluation.mechanism_detail: the session had closed when the API returned
evaluation.reason: precondition not established: the top-level transaction was aborted before it ended: at `before-end` the session was "idle in transaction (aborted)" and pg_xact_status() already reported it aborted (state: "idle in transaction"; pg_xact_status: in progress); PostgreSQL did not commit the transaction (pg_xact_status: committed; marker visible: true)

controls.detail: CTL-01.commit and CTL-01.rollback PASSed for efcore (native)

case_controls.detail: pg-control (correct) expected PASS, got PASS, pg-control (unsafe) expected FAIL, got FAIL

reproduction.requires: pnpm run setup, then pnpm run pg:up (README.md)
